evm.title: Mock polling booth
evm.intro: Walk through voting exactly as it happens on polling day. Nothing here is recorded, and no real party is on the ballot.
evm.stage.arrivalNarration: The first polling officer finds your name on the electoral roll and checks your photo ID. Show your EPIC card.
evm.stage.arrivalDone: Your name is on the roll.
evm.stage.inkNarration: The second officer marks your left index finger with indelible ink. It will not wash off for weeks, and it stops anyone voting twice.
evm.stage.ballotNarration: Inside the voting compartment the officer releases the ballot. Press the blue button beside the candidate of your choice. The last row is NOTA.
evm.stage.ballotHint: These candidates and symbols are invented for this tutorial.
evm.stage.vvpatNarration: You heard a beep and the red light came on. The VVPAT prints a slip showing your choice. It stays visible for seven seconds, then falls into a sealed box.
evm.stage.vvpatDropped: The slip has dropped into the sealed box.
evm.stage.doneNarration: Your vote is counted electronically from the control unit. The paper slips stay sealed and are counted only if the Commission orders a verification.
learn.title: Learn
learn.subtitle: The electoral process, in the order you meet it.
learn.step.turning18Body: You become eligible once you are 18 on the qualifying date. Eligibility is not automatic enrolment — you still have to apply.
learn.step.registerBody: File Form 6 online at the Voter Services Portal or on paper with your Booth Level Officer. Attach proof of age and address.
learn.step.epicBody: Once your application is accepted, the Commission issues your voter card with a unique number.
learn.step.checkRollBody: Search for your name before polling day. A card without a roll entry will not get you a ballot.
learn.step.findBoothBody: Your booth is assigned by address. Confirm it in advance so you are not searching on the day.
learn.step.pollingDayBody: Carry photo ID, get the ink mark, press the button, check the VVPAT slip.
learn.step.resultsBody: Votes are counted from the control units. Live results are published by the Commission.
learn.eligibility.intro: Five short questions. Nothing you answer leaves this device.
learn.eligibility.q.citizen: Are you a citizen of India?
learn.eligibility.q.registered: Is your name already on the electoral roll?
learn.eligibility.q.moved: Have you moved to a different constituency since you registered?
learn.eligibility.q.detailsCorrect: Are your name, address and photo on the roll correct?
learn.eligibility.notEligible: You are not eligible to enrol yet.
learn.eligibility.notEligibleBody: Enrolment requires Indian citizenship and an age of 18 on the qualifying date. Come back when both apply.
learn.eligibility.needsForm6Body: You are eligible but not yet on the roll, or you have moved constituency. Form 6 is the application for both.
learn.eligibility.needsForm8Body: You are on the roll but your details need correcting. Form 8 handles corrections and card replacement.
learn.eligibility.allGoodBody: Check the roll again close to polling day, then confirm your booth.
learn.eligibility.checkRollFirstBody: Search for your name on the Voter Services Portal, then come back and answer again.
learn.documents.intro: Tick these off as you gather them. Your ticks stay on this device.
learn.glossary.intro: Terms you will meet, explained plainly.
learn.quiz.intro: Ten questions. The explanation after each answer is the point, not the score.
learn.quiz.question: Question {n} of {total}
learn.q1: What is the minimum age to enrol as a voter in India?
learn.q1.exp: You must be 18 on the qualifying date to be enrolled.
learn.q2: Which form do you file to enrol as a new voter?
learn.q2.exp: Form 6 is the application for new enrolment and for shifting constituency.
learn.q3: How long is the VVPAT slip visible?
learn.q3.exp: The slip stays visible for seven seconds, then drops into a sealed box.
learn.q4.b: That you voted but chose no candidate
learn.q4.exp: NOTA records your participation while rejecting every candidate listed.
learn.q5: Is an EPIC card alone enough to vote?
learn.q5.b: No, your name must also be on the electoral roll
learn.q5.exp: Without a roll entry you will not be issued a ballot, card or no card.
learn.q6: Which finger gets the indelible ink mark?
learn.q6.exp: The mark goes on the left index finger and lasts for weeks.
learn.q7: Where is the ballot unit kept?
learn.q7.exp: The ballot unit sits in the voting compartment so your choice stays secret.
learn.q8: Can you take a phone into the voting compartment?
learn.q8.c: Only if it is switched off
learn.q8.exp: Phones and cameras are not allowed inside. The ballot is secret.
learn.q9: What is the national voter helpline number?
learn.q9.exp: Dial 1950 from anywhere in India for help with the electoral roll.
learn.q10.exp: The Election Commission of India is the independent body that conducts elections.
ins.title: Insights
ins.subtitle: Published election data, and how the machine is put together.
ins.turnoutBody: Share of registered electors who voted in each general election.
ins.anatomy: How an EVM is put together
ins.anatomyBody: Three units, connected by cable. The officer controls one; you only ever touch the ballot unit.
ins.anatomy.control: Control unit — held by the polling officer, who releases one ballot at a time.
ins.anatomy.ballot: Ballot unit — inside the voting compartment, with one blue button per candidate.
ins.anatomy.vvpat: VVPAT — prints the slip you verify, then seals it in a box.
ins.do1: Carry your EPIC card or another notified photo ID.
ins.do2: Check the VVPAT slip before you leave the compartment.
ins.do3: Ask the polling officer if anything is unclear.
ins.dont1: Do not take a phone or camera into the compartment.
ins.dont3: Do not accept anything offered in exchange for your vote.
